title: One Tree — the input architecture
summary: Collapse the app's 16 hand-written per-surface pointer-dispatch functions into one tree walk; fixes the toast pointer bug and makes any layer (incl. plugin overlays) receive input.
description:
The app delivers pointer input through 16 hand-written per-surface dispatch functions (heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs: 8 chrome + 4 pane-header + 3 pane-viewport; plus dispatch_modal_pointer) and has NO input pass for ordinary layers at all — heca/src/chrome/layers_glue.rs runs rebuild/layout/paint and never input.

This phase collapses that into ONE retained tree with one dispatch/layout/paint/hint walk, using the capture→target→bubble traversal heca-grid-ui already provides (`dispatch()` in heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs). Overlays, modals and pane headers become nodes; adding a surface becomes adding a child. Done properly this DELETES the 16 functions rather than adding a 17th.

═══ ⚠️ A WIDGET NEVER HAS TO BE NAMED — read this before adding any capability here ═══
(2026-09-01, after making exactly this mistake in T496.)

`key` is OPTIONAL and always has been. A widget that declares none still HAS an identity: it is
DERIVED from its content — its name within the nearest keyed ancestor, then a per-scope index among
identically-named siblings — never from its position in the tree, because a positional one moves
whenever anything else changes. `nav::identity_of` is that answer; `docs/widgets.md` § "Everything
else gets an identity anyway" is the rule, written long before this phase.

So a capability keyed to identity must NEVER be gated on `Base::key` being present. I wrote
`.draggable()` to read `key` directly, which silently did nothing on every widget that had no reason
to be named, and forced an author to learn an internal rule before they could drag anything.
Antonio: *"this makes developers know about an internal API not common"* and *"we decided earlier
that key is optional. Each widget/component should autogenerate this value if possible."*

THE RULE FOR ANY NEW CAPABILITY THAT NEEDS TO KNOW *WHICH* WIDGET: take the declared `key` when
there is one, fall back to the derived identity when there is not. In this phase's code that is
`drag::resolve::drag_identity`, and it is deliberately ONE function read by both the gesture and the
resolution so they cannot disagree. Guard: `an_unnamed_widget_is_still_draggable`.

Why the declared key is used unscoped while the derived one is scoped: a right-click and a drag must
point at the same thing, and `nav::key_at` answers a right-click with the row's OWN name. The
derived identity is scoped by keyed ancestors (`col:1/pane:2`) because that is what keeps a
remembered hint letter on the right row when two docks show the same rows.

═══ WHY THIS IS FIRST, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NOTIFICATION PHASE ═══
Moved from F009 to F003 on 2026-08-28 — it was never notification-specific; notifications are only where it surfaced. It sits at the top of F003 because it is the foundation Antonio's FIRST RULE rests on: a component cannot own its own input until one dispatch walks the tree.

TWO SILENT FAILURES IN TWO DAYS, one new surface, two different subsystems:
1. The toast stack receives zero pointer events, so its × and action buttons never fire and hover falls through to the pane beneath.
2. `prefix+/` lettered ONLY the toast — the hint walk read every visible layer's root box as an occluder, and a ToastStack is Pct(1.0) square because it POSITIONS its cards, not because it covers the screen. Fixed 2026-08-28 by reading the layer's own `covers_content` declaration, which the action router already honoured and the hint walk did not.

That is the shape of the defect: rebuild, layout, paint, hints and input are five separate walks over the layer stack, each with its own idea of what a layer means, and nothing checking they agree. Every new surface — a plugin's overlay included — must get it right in each one, and gets no error when it does not.

⚠️ AND THE SAME SHAPE ONE LEVEL DOWN (T495, 2026-09-01): a surface's BOX was taken for its input area. A box is routinely bigger than what a surface draws — a notification stack spans the window so a corner means the SCREEN's corner — so an empty invisible surface swallowed every press in the app and the chrome beneath stopped answering the mouse, with nothing failing anywhere. Now a seated surface passes the pointer through where it covers nothing (the browser's `pointer-events: none` on a positioned wrapper); its children still take what lands on them, and one that means to swallow says so through `overlay_occludes`, which `Overlay::blocking(true)` answers for the whole viewport. The seat sets that, so no author writes it and none can get it wrong.

═══ THE AUTHORITY ═══
`docs/surface-compositor.md` § 0 — the whole picture, and what AGENTS.md already flags as required reading before adding any layer or surface. Read it before planning any task here.

DONE 2026-08-28: `docs/input-architecture.md` was folded into it whole (now a redirect stub) so there is one voice rather than two, and AGENTS.md § 0d carries the FIRST RULE.

⚠️ CORRECTION: an earlier version of this description said `docs/hint-architecture.md` asserts "No second dispatch path" and that this is false. It is NOT false. Read in context, that sentence is about a **pick** propagating through the existing walk rather than introducing its own — which is correct. It is *pointer* input that has sixteen paths, not the picker.

═══ SCOPE, AND WHAT IS NOT HERE ═══
Priority order: T494+T495 (layer roots as tree children, modal as a swallowing node) landed first — both DONE and driven. Then T496 (chrome's 8 functions), T497 (pane header), T499 (HintSurface collapses to a tree path — 25 match sites across four files).

**T498 is CANCELED.** "Terminal viewport becomes a leaf node" duplicated P094(F011)/T449 from the input end. P097 owns the dispatch; P094 owns the terminal, and P094 depends on this phase.

T501/T502 are the plugin-capability half: a described plugin overlay gets input for free once this lands, but it still cannot BUILD what the exposé builds. Until one of our own overlays is built the way a plugin must build it (T502), "plugins can add overlays" is a claim, not a fact.

⚠️ MUST NOT be interleaved with the oversized-file splits — T466/T468/T470/T471/T472 carve up the same files (component.rs's router, event.rs, app/interaction.rs) and are deferred until this lands.

VERIFICATION: input routing is exactly where green tests prove nothing — the toast received no events for an unknown time and nothing errored. Antonio drives every surface's mouse behaviour (T500).

decisions: A surface is PLACED, never registered: chrome::place_surface puts it in the window root, keyed, replacing in place under the same key; chrome::remove_surface takes it out.

The window root lives on AppState, is NOT an Option, and the chrome is its child 0 rather than the root itself — the chrome is rebuilt on resize/sidebar-toggle/theme-reload and dropped outright by reload_config, so a surface parented to it would lose its open state, its half-played arrival and its focus.
seat_chrome finds the chrome slot BY KEY, not by position: a surface may be placed before the first chrome exists (the toast mounts at startup) and a positional child 0 would seat the chrome over it.

InteractionSource::Surface carries a SurfaceKey derived from the key a surface declares, not a LayerId — a registry id stops existing once a surface is a node, and a plugin can declare a key but can never obtain a LayerId. Derived from what the caller holds rather than looked up, because a surface builds its emitter BEFORE registering.

The registry keeps ONLY name, nesting, modality, covers_content, visibility and the ViewNode a described surface was described by. The live tree is a child of the window root, found by chrome::surface_node(_mut).
THE TREE TICKS; THE REGISTRY ONLY RECONCILES — leaving_before_tick() before window_root.tick(dt), retire_finished_exits() after. The registry must never advance a surface again.
The frost is Overlay::frosted(true), recorded into the scene's BASE band (never the deferred overlay band) and performed by the host between the base flush and the overlay band.
A context menu no longer swallows clicks page-wide: with a menu open, a click on a pane dismisses the menu AND focuses that pane. Antonio: 'current behavior is ok for me'. Do not fix back.
A widget never has to be named: key is optional and an identity is derived from content when none is declared. Never gate a capability on Base::key being present.
A seated surface passes the pointer through where it covers nothing; one that means to swallow says so through overlay_occludes, which Overlay::blocking(true) answers.
A placement's Auto axis is not an answer: the seat says where a surface goes and leaves the size to the surface.
Drag identity is the row's own name; the opaque DragItemId and the closed DragSurfaceId list are deleted from the widget layer.
An unclaimed drop goes to a host sink, like an unclaimed right-click — never an on_drop copied into each provider file.
A target declares what it takes and whether 'onto' means anything: a reorder is two halves, a pane onto a pane keeps three bands.
Dragging a workspace is out of scope: nothing can reorder workspaces and there is no action for it.

PaintCx::with_theme was proposed and rejected: the two themes are one theme with five values replaced, the shell already styles itself, and with_control_tone already does the inheritance. Do not retry it.
Moving a container's cursor is Global, not ContainerFocused: it changes no pane, column or layout, so clicking a sidebar row now moves the keyboard cursor to it like a file manager tree.
Modifiers are global device state held by the framework and stamped onto every pointer event; no host call site attaches them and no widget keeps a private copy.
What a drop does (move or swap) is the drag API's single decision, and which modifier means swap is a user setting rather than a constant in the widget library.
ButtonGroup reads the layout and never measures — Antonio, 2026-09-03: it must adapt to the available space like a CSS flex property.
The picker's compact-target rule stays: a small target keeps its smaller cap.
Which actions are destructive is the action's own declaration, read from the catalog, never a name match in a surface.
A widget is never added to a tree while that tree is being laid out — it has no bounds yet and paints at the window origin.
A named variant is the whole look, frame included — no container takes it away (Antonio: the UI style dictates that danger is framed).
Nothing is painted before the layout has given it a box, and revealing a hidden widget clears its layout node — one rule replacing three separate flicker patches.
One letter per thing, not per layer: a wrapper and the single node it holds share one, a real container's children each keep their own, and within one thing a declaration outranks mere actionability.
A boundary move is a transfer — both sides change by equal and opposite amounts — and the clamp is worked out once from whichever side runs out first.
Room for a new pane is made when it is ADDED, never inside the shared height distribution, which runs on every drag too.

An icon-only button refuses to shrink, declared on the button so any container gets it, and the re-measure only ever tightens — it never writes the relaxed value back over a container's own declaration.
The command line declares its arguments with the action system's own ArgDescriptor and checks them with the same check_args, so one idea of 'what arguments does this take' serves both.

A menu is a DECLARATION on any node, never a widget kind — natively it is one builder on any widget, so a described node says it the same way, and adding a ContextMenu kind would be the second path this closed.

lock replaces covers_content: it means 'what is behind me is unreachable', not pixels — the expose covers every pixel it draws over and still sets it false. Named surfaces (Dialog, ContextMenu, CommandPalette) set it themselves, so no call site writes it.

Taking the keyboard is never declared — a surface that wants keys holds focus, and every layer widget binds its open signal to it. A true-by-default flag was rejected: it would make a toast the active context and blank every letter.

tasks.title: Layer roots become children of the one tree
tasks.description:
GOAL: every registered surface is a node in the single retained tree, so the existing capture→target→bubble walk delivers pointer input to it.

═══ STATE 2026-08-31: SHIPPED, WITH ONE OPEN REGRESSION ═══

**The reported toast bug is FIXED and verified on screen by Antonio** — the × closes, action buttons fire, hover no longer falls through to the pane beneath.

Commits, in order:
- `f5f2262` — the frost became a surface property (`Overlay::frosted`) and the window root was introduced. `RetainedChrome` holds only what a chrome *build* produced; `AppState::window_root` is the one retained tree and is not an Option, because the chrome is rebuilt on resize/sidebar-toggle/theme-reload and dropped outright by `reload_config` — a surface parented to any of that would be destroyed with it.
- `0c45480` — the toast stack placed via `chrome::place_surface` instead of registered. `InteractionSource::Surface` carries a `SurfaceKey` (derived from the key a surface declares) instead of a `LayerId`, because a registry id stops existing once a surface is a node. `AppState::notification_layer_id` and `LayerId::for_test` deleted with their last callers.
- `971b1e2` — **the remaining three surfaces** (exposé, command palette, `OverlayHost` modals + context menus). Trees moved into the window root; `LayerRegistry` keeps name/nesting/modality/`covers_content`. Deleted: `layout_layers`, `paint_layers`, the separate layer scene and its second `render_chrome` flush, `DynamicLayer::root`/`root_mut`/`opacity`/`is_leaving`, `visible_roots_mut`, `top_modal_root_mut`, `LayerContent`.

Gate green throughout (667 heca tests; clippy at the two known pre-existing warnings).

═══ ⚠️ OPEN REGRESSION — Antonio, driving, 2026-08-31 ═══

Introduced by `971b1e2`. **The exposé's animation:**
1. Zoom-OUT stalls at roughly 10–15% opacity.
2. **Moving the mouse completes it** — so nothing is requesting the next frame, and any input event kicks it. That is a frame-scheduling symptom, not an animation-maths one.
3. After the first open, subsequent zoom-INs show the same stall.
4. After that, `ctrl+h/j/k/l` are broken too.

PRIME SUSPECT, unverified — instrument before changing code:
- **A hidden surface is still a child of the window root.** `layout_layers`/`paint_layers` used to filter on `visible`, so a hidden layer was inert. Now its node stays in the tree: it is still ticked, still walked, and can still hold `Base::focused` — which would explain (4), the keys going to a surface that is not on screen.
- **Double tick.** `heca/src/app/lifecycle.rs:111` `state.window_root.tick(dt)` now ticks every surface as a child, and `:127` `state.layers.tick(&mut state.window_root, dt)` ticks them again. Two advances per frame, and the registry's `was_leaving`/`still_leaving` transition is read around only one of them — so the frame an exit *finishes* can be missed, and with it the `fading = true` that requests the frame which paints its absence.

Both are consequences of the same thing: the registry's tick was written when it owned the trees and nothing else walked them.

VERIFY (Antonio drives; green tests prove nothing here): exposé open/close animation over several cycles, `ctrl+h/j/k/l` inside a dialog after an exposé cycle, the context menu, the confirm dialog, the command palette, and `prefix+/` landing on the front surface only.

═══ NOT IN THIS TASK ═══
`T495` (modal as a node that swallows) is still open: modal **keyboard** still routes through `LayerRegistry::top_modal_node_mut` rather than the tree walk, and `dispatch_modal_pointer` still exists.

═══ DONE — 2026-08-31, driven on screen by Antonio ═══

**The reported bug is fixed and verified:** the toast's × closes it, its action buttons fire, hover no longer falls through to the pane beneath, and `prefix+Enter` still splits with a toast up.

Every surface — the toast stack, the exposé, the command palette, `OverlayHost` modals and context menus — is now a child of `AppState::window_root`. One walk lays them out, paints them, delivers their pointer events and collects their hint letters.

**THE ARCHITECTURE IS IN `docs/surface-compositor.md` § 0**, which was rewritten to the built state. It is not restated here; a second copy drifts. § 0.6 is what changed and how to place a surface; § 0.7 is the tick rule below; § 0.5 is the record-and-perform seam; § 9 is the registry, now marked history.

COMMITS: `f5f2262` (frost becomes a surface property; window root introduced) · `0c45480` (toast placed; `InteractionSource::Surface` carries a `SurfaceKey`) · `971b1e2` (the remaining three surfaces; 811 insertions, 448 deletions, 20 files) · `a34ca0b` (the regression fix below).

DELETED, not moved: `layout_layers`, `paint_layers`, the separate layer scene **and its second `render_chrome` flush**, `DynamicLayer::root`/`root_mut`/`opacity`/`is_leaving`, `visible_roots_mut`, `top_modal_root_mut`, `LayerContent`, `LayerBackdrop`/`set_backdrop`/`wants_frost`/`frost_opacity`, `AppState::notification_layer_id`, `LayerId::for_test`.

═══ THE REGRESSION — FOUND AND FIXED (`a34ca0b`) ═══

**It is fixed. Do not go looking for it.** Recorded because the rule it left behind is load-bearing.

Antonio drove `971b1e2` and found: the exposé's zoom-out stalled around 10–15% opacity; moving the mouse completed it; subsequent zoom-ins did the same; afterwards `ctrl+h/j/k/l` were broken.

One cause. Once surfaces became children of the window root, `window_root.tick(dt)` advanced them as children — and `LayerRegistry::tick` advanced them again, reading `was_leaving` *after* the tree's tick had already consumed the transition. On the frame an exit finished the registry saw "was not leaving", never set `visible = false`, never set `fading`, never requested the frame that paints the absence. The surface stayed visible and still modal, which is why the keys died.

**THE RULE: the tree ticks; the registry only reconciles.** `leaving_before_tick()` before `window_root.tick(dt)`, `retire_finished_exits()` after. The registry must never advance a surface again.

**The test gap that let it through:** the registry tests called `reg.tick(...)` directly and never ran the tree walk doing the second advance. They now call a `frame(reg, window, dt)` helper (`heca/src/chrome/layers/tests.rs`) that runs the real order. Keep it that way.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══

Antonio drove all of it: the toast's × and action buttons, hover not falling through, `prefix+Enter` with a toast up, and the exposé's open/close animation after the fix ("it works"). Gates green throughout — 667 heca tests plus the other crates, clippy at the two known pre-existing `toast/stack.rs:80` warnings.

═══ NOT IN THIS TASK ═══

`T495` — modal as a node that swallows — is still open and unstarted. `dispatch_modal_pointer` still exists in `heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs`, and modal **keyboard** still routes through `LayerRegistry::top_modal_node_mut` in `heca/src/app/events.rs` rather than the tree walk. Antonio flagged modal keyboard (Tab/Shift+Tab in a Dialog, Ctrl+h/j/k/l, Esc, scrim-click, `prefix+/` onto a dialog button) as the highest-risk area after this migration — that is T495's to verify.

Reason: T494 cannot land before the scene seam exists. The frost backdrop blurs whatever is behind an exposé, and needs a point in the frame where the scene holds everything beneath the surface and nothing of it. That point exists today only because chrome and layers paint into two separate scenes. Move layers into one tree and they paint in one continuous walk — the moment disappears and the frost breaks the instant T494 lands, unless a node can first say "blur what is behind me here" and let the host perform it. That is exactly this task's seam.
What was being done: Read only, no code. Established: (1) the task's stated approach — chrome root owns the layers, or a window root above both — fights the registry's design; (2) the registry is itself a parallel tree, storing parent links and re-deriving nesting every frame via z_path, duplicating what child position gives free; (3) blast radius is 21 LayerId references across 8 files and 18 layer-root accesses across 6; (4) the `Overlay` widget already provides everything the registry does — modal capture, fall-through, show/hide, animation, keyboard, occlusion geometry, and nesting — except reach outside the chrome tree; (5) the layout engine already supports absolutely-positioned children that take no space, so layers as stacked children need no new layout capability. All of it is written up in docs/surface-compositor.md § 0 and committed (9f40fb7), together with heca/tests/surface_drift.rs, which fails the build when a new surface is registered instead of placed.
Resume location: heca/src/chrome/layers_glue.rs (the three passes, no input pass); heca/src/chrome/dispatch.rs:28 (dispatch_modal_pointer, the only layer input path); heca/src/app/events.rs (the hand-ordered pointer sequence); heca/src/app/render.rs:1045-1075 (the frost pass that forces the ordering).
How to resume: Do T448 first. Then rewrite this task against the real plan rather than its current text: overlays become ordinary children (the Overlay widget already handles modal capture, fall-through, nesting, animation and keyboard), the registry shrinks to a name-to-node lookup so show_layer/hide_layer keep working, and input becomes one walk from the root. FIRST ATTEMPT WAS AIMED ONE NODE TOO LOW and did not fix it: giving ToastStack an honest hit area (cards only) left the app broken, because what the pointer actually meets is the KeyHintGroup wrapped around the stack at mount (chrome/notification_layer.rs), and that wrapper HUGS its child — so it inherited the window-sized box. Verified to fail without the widget fix. ⚠️ That is the lesson of the first attempt: a guard for a seating must construct what the app actually seats, or it certifies a shape nobody runs.

A box that is bigger than what the widget draws is a lie that no amount of correcting the derived answers can undo, and every node stacked on top of it inherits the lie. Do not take the viewport in order to position something in a corner; be the size of what you draw, and move.

tasks.title: Chrome's 8 dispatch functions collapse into the walk
tasks.description:
GOAL: delete the 8 chrome_dispatch_* wrappers and route chrome pointer/widget input through the single tree walk.

═══ COMMITTED, driven and confirmed ═══
e441d9c — a row is dragged by the NAME IT ALREADY DECLARES. `.draggable()` / `.drop_target()` take no argument. Deleted the opaque `DragItemId` and the closed `DragSurfaceId`. ⚠️ NEVER gate a capability on `Base::key` being present — guard `an_unnamed_widget_is_still_draggable`.
966cc98 — an unclaimed drop is handed to the host ONCE, through `drag::install_drop_sink`.
5d69f4a — THE ROW OWNS THE GESTURE, IN EVERY SIDEBAR. A drop is TOLD what it landed on; `draggable_as` / `accepts` are free words so a plugin invents its own.
2019b22 — MARK THE NODE THE WALK FOUND. `DropHit` carries its path. Plus `accepts_beside`, the carried subtree skipped, the source fading.
161c329 — the framework answers whether a drag is in flight (`heca_grid_ui::dragging(root)` via `chrome::drag_in_flight`). ⚠️ THIS COMMIT SHIPPED A BUG — see below.

═══ UNCOMMITTED, GREEN, ALL DRIVEN AND CONFIRMED BY ANTONIO ═══
1. THE OLD DRAG MACHINE IS DELETED (868 net lines). Gone from heca-grid-ui: drag/{context,item,state,math}.rs — DragContext, DragItemId, DragSurfaceId, SurfaceDragState, DragLabel, DragPhase, rubberband, DEFAULT_DRAG_THRESHOLD_SQ (the new gesture has its own threshold in pointer.rs). drag/mod.rs is resolve + sink only. Gone from heca: mouse/drag.rs and mouse/target.rs entirely; AppDragPayload, drag_ctx, pending_click_action (never written) off AppState; paint_drag_overlay + its render.rs call; DragSourceKind / target_accepted_by / resolve_sidebar_drop / sidebar_drop_target; the three sidebar release entry points; the drag_ctx.active_surface branch. The TEMPORARY position-based resolution in mouse/target.rs died with it. The enum dispatch collapsed to direct calls. mouse/drag.rs's router held only interactive move once the sidebar handlers went, so it moved into interactive.rs. SCOPE HELD: interactive_move and divider resizing untouched.

2. ⚠️ REGRESSION FIXED — from 161c329, found by driving. The move that DRIVES a drag was gated on `!drag_in_flight`. The old guard asked whether the APP's machine was dragging — always false since the row took over — so the dispatch always ran. Re-pointing it at the tree made it truthful, and truthful broke it: the tree got no moves for the whole gesture, so the preview froze where it was picked up and DragOver never ran (no side, no mark). Only the threshold-crossing move got through. FIX: the window tree is ALWAYS fed the move; the pane header/viewport trees (separate trees a window-root drag does not reach) stay gated. Hover was the gate's reason and the framework already clears it under a drag.

3. ⚠️ MODIFIERS HAD NO HOME — the reason swap never happened. RawPointer::new defaults modifiers to empty and the Event::pointer_* constructors never stamp them, so every event the chrome_dispatch_* family sent carried "nothing held" and the drop always read Move. Meanwhile Input, Dialog and CommandPalette EACH kept a private copy of the ModifiersChanged broadcast. FIX AT LIBRARY LEVEL: the framework remembers the modifier state (`event::modifiers()`, recorded in `dispatch` from the broadcast the host already sends) and `pointer::route` stamps every pointer event with it. Deleted: the host's stamping, PointerState::drag_mods, and all three widget copies.

4. WHAT A DROP DOES IS ONE DECISION — `drag::DropAction` {Move, Swap}, `DropAction::held()`. "Shift means swap" was written twice (the framework's paint AND the host's drop handling) and they could disagree — which is exactly what was seen. Now the paint asks it, `Dropped` carries it, and the host reads `dropped.action`.

5. THE SWAP MODIFIER IS DATA — `drag::set_swap_rule` (same shape as install_drop_sink), default Shift. A binding is not a constant compiled into a widget library.

6. THE THREE REMAINING READINGS point at DropAction::held() (mouse/interactive.rs x2, mouse/surface_left.rs). No reading of Shift-as-swap survives outside the drag API.

tasks.description:
GOAL (met): the pane's info bar stopped being a separate thing the app drew and routed by hand, and became part of the pane itself. DONE 2026-09-04 — Antonio drove and confirmed every fix.

⚠️ THE RECORD IS IN THE DOCS, not here. `.planner/docs/t497-open-issues.md` carries every defect with its REAL cause and the guard now holding it, disproved diagnoses marked ❌, and the three extra fixes in full. `.planner/docs/t497-header-buttons.md` carries what was built and THE API SURFACE ADDED, every builder and token by name. `.planner/docs/session-2026-09-04-cli-and-resize-edges.md` carries the resize-edge and command-line work, which Antonio asked for during this task and which has NO TASK OF ITS OWN.

WHAT SHIPPED: ButtonGroup (a row of actions that fits its space, reading the layout and never measuring); tooltips as a property of every widget; the picker's letters with their own size and colour; buttons gained a held-on state, a tone and an icon-only form; destructiveness became the action's own declaration.

THE SIX DEFECTS — and every one had a different cause than the one recorded. That is the lesson of this task. Not one written diagnosis survived a measurement; what worked every time was reproducing it in a harness and printing numbers.
1. Destructive border — CLOSED BY ANTONIO'S DECISION: the style dictates that danger is framed. The strip-it attempt was removed at the widget level, so no container can take a named variant away.
2. Corner flicker — a widget revealed or created during the layout walk keeps zero bounds at the origin, and an icon draws at font size wherever its box claims to be. Fixed centrally: revealing clears the layout node, and nothing is painted before it has a box. One rule replacing three patches.
3. The dots button was a 4-8px sliver — the only child not told to refuse shrinking. Fixed on Button itself, so a plain Flex is right too.
4. Its picker letter — followed from 3 and from the letters rule below.
5. "Third pane off screen" — NOTHING WAS EVER PUSHED. The heights always summed to the column, which is why an earlier measurement found them correct and stopped. The new pane was STARVED to one pixel. Room is now made when a pane is ADDED, never inside the shared distribution.
6. Divider shimmer — LEFT AS IS on Antonio's decision. Diagnosed with a probe he ran: no blank frame, both panes re-render fully every step, and the shimmering pane is the one LOSING rows. It is the terminal's own reflow. The recorded "jitter in pane heights" cause is disproved.

Its PAINT stays special — it still renders through the GPU terminal path (heca-renderer, cosmic-text atlas), not a Scene DrawCommand list. - Panes are GPU terminal surfaces, not grid-ui widgets. events.rs MouseInput/CursorMoved/MouseWheel route to the terminal via forward_mouse_button / forward_mouse_move / forward_mouse_wheel (heca/src/app/terminal_host.rs) AFTER a chain of early-return checks (modal, pane-header button, viewport widget, divider resize).

- heca/src/mouse/ owns hit_test_pane, on_cursor_moved, on_mouse_input, resize gestures, interactive-move, edge scroll.

tasks.description:
GOAL: the prefix+/ hint system stops enumerating surfaces and walks the one tree. Delete the HintSurface enum arms and the ~25 match sites that each list the roots.

CURRENT STATE (heca/src/chrome/hint/):
- hint/surfaces.rs — ~12 match sites over a HintSurface enum (one arm per surface: chrome, panes, each layer kind, pane header, ...).
- hint/targets.rs — ~7 match sites collecting hint targets per surface.
- hint/visibility.rs — ~4 match sites deciding which surface's hints are shown (e.g. "not the sidebar while a pane is zoomed or a toast is up").
- hint/letters.rs — ~2 match sites assigning letters.
- Total ~25 sites. Adding a surface means adding an arm to each; a miss is a silently un-hintable surface.
- The layer stack already models occlusion as tree position ("z is a path, not a band"); hint visibility should read the same tree, not a parallel enum.
- NOTE (heca-57, 2026-08-27): the sidebar hint-letter instability is ALREADY FIXED on the grid-ui side and is NOT part of this task. Cause was naming: a container declared with scope_key (what a dock does) contributed nothing to its children's names because the naming fn read only key, so two docks holding the same workspace produced identical name sets and a remembered letter bounced between copies. Fixed centrally in heca-grid-ui — a widget now has one declared name (key, else scope_key) and every namer reads it (also closed T482). Do not re-investigate letter stability here.

WORK:
- Once input is one tree walk (tasks 1-5), hint collection is one walk too: descend the tree, collect every hintable node (Base already carries hintable + the pick intent since the cards went into the tree), in paint order, honouring occlusion by tree position.
- Replace HintSurface with a tree path / node handle. hint/surfaces.rs, targets.rs, letters.rs collapse to a single traversal.
- hint/visibility.rs rules ("hide the sidebar's hints while a covering layer is up") become "a node occluded by a covering sibling is not collected" — read from the tree, not special-cased per surface.
- KeyHintGroup / the notification.pick precise picker (heca/src/chrome/notification_layer.rs wraps the stack in a KeyHintGroup bound to notification_pick_open) still works — it is a sub-scope within the same walk.

PRESERVE: prefix+/ letters on every clickable chrome button, on toast action buttons and the x, on pane-picker targets; the KeyHint being a UNIVERSAL overlay for any clickable widget (never column/ws/pane-specific); a covering overlay hiding the hints of what it covers.

VERIFY: Antonio drives — prefix+/ with the sidebar open, with a toast up, with a modal up, with the exposé open; confirm the letter set is correct in each and that occluded targets get no letter.

~0.5 day. Do after the input tasks land (it depends on the tree being the source of truth).

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-09-05, commit 4cb7e24 on feat/hint-collapses-to-the-tree (29 files, +982/-331). Branch cut from main at 069e3b3; T497 and everything beside it merged as PR #263 first.

SHIPPED
- The parallel enum is gone. HintSurface is Window + Pane(PaneId); the Layer arm and its match sites went with it, and so did the second walk over every registered layer.
- THE DEFECT IT WAS CAUSING, measured not inferred: Chrome resolved to the window root and Layer(id) to a CHILD of that same root, so every seated surface's widgets were collected TWICE (once at their path from the root, once from the layer) and one button carried two candidates. A throwaway probe showed a root holding a seated surface answering collect_hints with [[0], [1, 0]] while the surface alone answered [[0]]. A surface the registry did not own (the toast stack, placed as heca.notifications) fitted no arm at all and was attributed to Chrome, judged by the chrome's occluders rather than its own.
- NEW LIBRARY CAPABILITY heca_grid_ui::collect_hints_by_surface -> Vec<SurfaceHints>: every pick target grouped by the surface that owns it, front to back, each group carrying that surface's path, key, laid-out bounds and declarations. Built ON collect_hints so the candidacy rules stay in one place. Three rules it now holds so no future host re-derives them: front-to-back is lexicographic on the path reversed; the page is the group with no path (so "page or surface" is structural, never a name match); a target belongs to the DEEPEST enclosing surface, so a menu inside a dialog groups under the menu and nobody assumes surfaces are direct children of the root.
- RULE ZERO closed. covers_content/modal were fields on the host registry passed as positional bools into add/insert/add_view/add_named; a plugin could declare them only by reaching a host call. Now: `lock` is a builder on the widget (Base::lock, ComponentExt::lock), and taking the keyboard is NOT declared at all - a surface that wants keys holds focus, every layer widget binds its open signal to Base::focused, so an open overlay is the active context by being open and an ambient one is not by holding no focus. heca_grid_ui::holds_keyboard exposes that; Base::captures_keyboard is an optional override (Option<bool>) for a surface the framework cannot read.
- RENAME covers_content -> lock (Antonio). The old name described pixels while meaning "what is behind me is unreachable" - the mismatch that made the expose map, which covers every pixel it draws over, refuse every act on the pane it exists to let you pick.
- ENCAPSULATION (Antonio): a named surface sets lock for itself - Dialog, ContextMenu and CommandPalette each in their own constructor. NO app call site writes it. Only raw Overlay takes the builder, which is the piece a plugin builds a new surface from. Confirmed Overlay accepts children natively and declaratively (impl Parent for Overlay in heca-view), and that the expose is itself built from Overlay + CardGrid - so a plugin already has everything; ExposeGrid stays app-side (it takes PaneId; § 0b-bis says a component moves up on the SECOND caller).
- open_view_layer lost its now-dead `modal` parameter.

VERIFICATION
- 1289 tests pass, 0 failures. Clippy exit 0 at the documented baseline (one pre-existing toast/stack.rs "very complex type" plus the third-party block v0.1.6 note). Every changed file's per-file rustfmt count at or below its pre-change value; four raises were introduced and hand-corrected.
- Six guards, EACH RUN AGAINST ITS OWN BUG: grouping, ordering (sort reversed), nesting (shallowest-wins), the plugin-facing declaration (dropped from the read-back), a surface that declares nothing, and liveness (filter removed).
- ONE GUARD WAS DISCARDED AS VACUOUS: the first grouping assertion checked the collected paths held no duplicates. Sabotage showed the double collection produces [[0], [0, 0], [1, 0]] - all distinct - so it passed with the bug fully present. Replaced with an exact-paths assertion and re-sabotaged.
- DRIVEN BY ANTONIO on the GPU app: letters visible at all, prefix+q pane-select, the expose with both prefix+/ and its own `s` picker, and toast letters. Four of the four scenarios the task named.

REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED WHILE DRIVING (Antonio: "Hint letters not visible anymore. None of them. Neither prefix+q shows letters")
Cause: hiding a surface calls node.hide() and leaves it SEATED - remove_surface runs only on destruction - so the tree is full of dismissed surfaces, and the command palette registers at startup as hidden + modal + covering. Reading its declarations without asking whether it was live broke the walk at a hidden modal from the moment the app launched, suppressing every letter everywhere. The old stack got liveness for free from visible_front_to_back, which filters on `visible`; walking the tree instead meant asking the tree for liveness too.
Fix: LayerRegistry::live_declaration_at / slot_is_live, which is is_active(is_leaving(..)) - the SAME expression content_covered already uses, so "is this surface in charge" has one answer. My first attempt was a `live()` predicate written at the call site in the hint module; its test failed (Component::hide is a default no-op a plain container ignores) and that is what sent me to the shared rule instead of shipping a duplicate.

REMAINING / UNVERIFIED
- NOT DRIVEN SINCE THE LOCK WORK. The registration path for every overlay, modal, menu and the palette changed after Antonio's last visual pass. Needs one more: open a dialog, a context menu, the command palette and the expose, and confirm prefix+/ letters stop at the surface in front and that a dismissed one suppresses nothing. This is T500's business.
- Panes remain a separate retained tree, so HintSurface still has two variants. It collapses to one in P094(F011)/T449.

FILES: heca-grid-ui/src/{component.rs, builders.rs, lib.rs, hint/{collect.rs, mod.rs, tests.rs}, widgets/{dialog.rs, context_menu.rs, command_palette.rs}}; heca/src/chrome/{hint/{surfaces,targets,letters,visibility}.rs, layers/{mod,layer,order,tests}.rs, overlay.rs, palette.rs, expose/mod.rs, notification_layer.rs}; docs/{widgets.md, surface-compositor.md, input-architecture.md}; AGENTS.md.

DOCS: docs/widgets.md documents collect_hints_by_surface with the code a caller writes and the lock-vs-holds_keyboard split; surface-compositor.md § 0.6 corrected - the registry's row now reads "name and nesting", since it no longer holds modality or coverage.

tasks.title: Regression pass — Antonio driving every surface
tasks.description:
GOAL: a structured interactive regression pass over every mouse and hint behaviour on every surface, driven by Antonio, after the plumbing tasks (layer roots, modal, chrome, pane header, terminal viewport, hint) land. This is not optional and green tests do not substitute for it — the pre-change design already failed silently (the toast received no input for an unknown length of time and nothing errored).

ABSORBS the former P060/T207 "Validate ToastStack overlay pass-through" (canceled — its pointer half was never implementation-free, it was this whole phase). The toast section below is T207's acceptance criteria in full.

CHECKLIST (Antonio drives each; a failure blocks the phase):
- Toast (was T207):
  - clicking the × closes the toast;
  - an action button fires its intent (and dismisses if dismiss_after);
  - clicking OUTSIDE any toast passes through to the UI/pane below — the toast consumes only the strip its cards cover;
  - hovering a toast does NOT highlight the pane beneath, and pauses/reveals the toast's own affordances;
  - a queued toast promotes when a visible one is dismissed;
  - prefix+Enter still splits a pane with a toast up, and other Global actions still route — a visible toast must NEVER put the app in Domain::Overlay. (This last invariant is ALREADY implemented and unit-tested — chrome/layers/tests.rs coverage_is_reported_only_while_the_layer_is_visible and app/interaction.rs coverage_still_decides_when_no_surface_holds_the_keyboard cover the toast's exact Persistent/modal:false/covers_content:false shape. Confirm it still holds after the tree work, don't re-derive it.)
- Modal: open the confirm dialog, click a button, Esc, scrim-click, Tab/Shift+Tab between buttons, Ctrl+h/l inside, prefix+/ onto a button, terminal sees no stray click while it is up.
- Sidebar: MarkerGroup grip hover cue, Row hover, click a row, scroll the sidebar, drag a column, drag the scrollbar thumb and release off it, right-click a row -> context menu.
- Pane header: each action button clicks + hovers, press the empty band (focuses, no selection), resize a divider under a header band.
- Terminal (longest): PTY mouse reporting into a TUI (htop/vim mouse), host-grid selection (click-drag, double/triple-click, shift-extend), scrollback wheel, click-to-focus, Ctrl/Cmd+wheel font zoom, edge auto-scroll during a pane drag, interactive-move modifier drag, vim Escape reaches the program.
- Hints: prefix+/ with sidebar / toast / modal / expose up — correct letter set each time, occluded targets get no letter.
- Exposé: still opens, cursor moves, cards activate, delete letters work.

OUTPUT: a short pass/fail note per line in the task completion, plus any follow-up tasks filed for failures. ~0.5-1 day of Antonio's time.

**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-09-05, driven by Antonio on the GPU app. This task was never opened in the planner while it was being carried out — he drove it, reported results, and I fixed what he found, then wrongly reported the task as closed. He noticed it was still 'planned' and asked why. Recording it now against what actually happened.

ANTONIO'S PASS — HIS RESULTS, VERBATIM WHERE HE GAVE THEM
- Toast: "toask all tests ok" — PASS. Absorbs the former P060/T207 acceptance criteria.
- Sidebar: "sidebar:on" — PASS.
- Context menu: "context menu:ok" — PASS.
- Sidebar context menu: "sidebar context menu: ok" — PASS.
- prefix+/ : "OK" — PASS.
- prefix+q : "ok" — PASS.
- Exposé: "expose: OK" — PASS. Also confirmed separately that it works with BOTH prefix+/ and its own `s` picker, which is the KeyHintGroup sub-scope case T499's PRESERVE clause names.
- Terminal: "after a command buttongour in the heade seems to re-render and flashes for a while" — FAIL, fixed (below).

TWO DEFECTS FOUND, BOTH FIXED IN 1b8a5b1

1. THE HEADER FLASHED AFTER A COMMAND. Diagnosed by instrumenting, not by reasoning — and my first read of the trace was WRONG. I called it an oscillating terminal; the second measurement showed it was four separate `ll` runs, each transitioning correctly. The terminal was never at fault.
   The real cause: one command rebuilt the whole header TWICE (command start, command end), and a rebuilt widget paints nothing until the layout walk gives it a box. Two causes inside that: `view.status` was part of the header's identity while being RENDERED NOWHERE in that bar (half the rebuilds, for something invisible), and the words — program name, branch, cwd — were part of its identity although they change constantly and change nothing about its shape.
   Fix: the words became a per-frame input written into the retained tree, exactly as the pane's own rect already is; only the SHAPE (which segments have data) still rebuilds. Library half: `set_text_by_key` — change what a named node says, addressed by its own key as hints already are.

2. THE FLASH SURVIVED, on focus change, on split, and when the cwd was detected. Antonio: "This should be something like react does… And this should be like this for every widgets", and "whenever i put a ButtonGroup it should have this problem fix without any responsibility for other developers/agents".
   Real cause, in ONE widget: `ButtonGroup` decides what fits by reading the layout that already happened, so its decision lands in `on_layout` — AFTER the pass that informed it — and the arrangement being replaced is painted once. Four symptoms, one widget, and no caller could have known or prevented it.
   Fix IN THE ENGINE, not in the widget's callers: `LayoutEngine::compute` now settles — a widget that changes what it holds in response to its layout asks for another pass and gets it before anything is painted. Bounded at three (`SETTLE_PASSES`), because `Display::Auto` can genuinely never settle: taking the words off makes the row fit, which is the condition for putting them back. `ButtonGroup` simply asks, as any widget would; every future widget that decides from its own layout gets this free.
   ⚠️ I started writing a FOURTH hand-rolled per-frame style writer beside `size_to`, `translate_tree` and `refresh_pane_header_text` before Antonio stopped me ("Damn you were going to do the stupid hardcoded way??? again???"). Three hand-written copies of a thing is the signal that the capability is missing — count them before writing another.

VERIFICATION
- Gates green: 1388 tests pass, clippy exit 0 at the documented baseline (one pre-existing toast/stack.rs "very complex type" plus the third-party block v0.1.6 note), no file's rustfmt count raised.
- Guards, each run against its own bug: one layout pass gives the same row as four, at four widths (sabotaged by removing the settle — red at 90px); the header's words and width never rebuild it while a vanished segment does (sabotaged by putting git_branch back in the key — red); a named node's words are rewritten in place (sabotaged by finding the node and writing nothing — red).
- ⚠️ THE BUTTON-GROUP TESTS LAID OUT FOUR TIMES — this defect was written into the test helpers, which is why they never saw it. They gave the group passes a real frame never does.
- ⚠️ A GUARD I WROTE WAS VACUOUS and only sabotage found it: the header-key assertion first sabotaged `cwd`, which is None in both fixtures, so it passed with the bug fully present. Re-sabotaged with the field the test actually varies.

REMAINING / UNVERIFIED — the reason this is worth reading before closing the phase
The layout settle (1b8a5b1) landed AFTER Antonio's last visual pass. He confirmed the button group was fixed *after a command*; he has NOT driven the settle itself. Gestures needed: change focus between panes, split, run a command in a fresh directory. Everything in d013f5c is also undriven, since the registration path for every overlay, modal, menu and the palette moved when `lock` moved onto the widgets.

FILES: heca-grid-ui/src/{layout.rs, component.rs, widgets/{button_group,label,tag}.rs, hint/{offer,mod,tests}.rs, lib.rs}; heca-grid-ui/tests/button_group.rs; heca/src/chrome/{pane/mod.rs, pane_header.rs, mod.rs}.

NO FOLLOW-UP TASKS FILED — both defects were fixed within this task, and Antonio decides what gets filed.

tasks.title: Declarative arms for the widgets a plugin overlay needs
tasks.description:
GOAL: close the described-widget coverage gap so a plugin can actually build an overlay, not just be promised one. This is the CAPABILITY half of plugin overlays — the plumbing half falls out of the one-tree work; this does not.

CURRENT STATE (verified in code):
- 13 of 46 grid-ui widgets have NO declarative (ViewNode) form: CardGrid, ChromeRegion, CommandPalette, ContextMenu, Dialog, FocusScope, KeyHint, NfIcon, Pane, Progress, Spinner, Tooltip, Visibility. (Name-based check across heca-view / heca-view-realize; CardGrid verified directly twice.)
- Some are host-only BY DESIGN and stay that way: ChromeRegion, Pane, FocusScope.
- CardGrid — the widget the exposé cursor is built on — has zero references in heca-view or heca-view-realize. A described tree cannot construct one today.
- The declarative path: heca/src/chrome/view.rs (ViewNode / WidgetKind), heca/src/chrome/realize.rs (the recursive host mapper), plus the widget's own arm. Precedent: Dialog::body_boxed for a realized subtree; Choice children for options.
